clue.text: Tree found by common — not yew, by the sound of it

indicators.note: 'not' tells you to take something away from the word for common

parts.note: common in the sense of widely liked or general

indicators.note: the yew is only the tree's name as heard, standing for the pronoun with that pronunciation

parts.note: yew is pronounced like you, which texting writes as the single letter U

explanation.surface: A walker spots a tree on the village common and notes it isn't a yew.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove the U from POPULAR. The tree and yew both point at arboreal answers, but yew only supplies a sound.
explanation.definitionFit: The poplar is a tall, fast-growing tree of the willow family.

clue.text: Page on execution finds agreement

parts.note: P is the standard abbreviation for page
execution as in carrying out a deed, an act

explanation.surface: A page boy facing execution manages to strike a deal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On' just places the page first; 'execution' is the doing of something, not a hanging.
explanation.definitionFit: A pact is a formal treaty or deal between parties.

clue.text: Totally absurd charge brought by minor

parts.note: a charge is the price asked
minor meaning smaller, lesser

explanation.surface: A ridiculous criminal charge brought against a child.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Minor' looks like a youngster in court; here it means smaller in amount. The answer's informal sense of hilariously ridiculous is the one defined.
explanation.definitionFit: Colloquially, something priceless is so ridiculous or funny that it beggars belief.

clue.text: A bike race round trees, originally

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the race goes round, enclosing the trees within it

parts.note: the TT, Tourist Trophy, is the Isle of Man motorcycle race
firs are conifer trees

explanation.surface: A cycle race once ran through woodland, in its early days.
explanation.walkthrough: The Isle of Man Tourist Trophy is a motorcycle race, not a bicycle one, but crosswords happily call it a bike race.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean in the beginning, before later developments took place.

clue.text: Quickly cut thick slice of meat

parts.note: to chop is to cut
a chop, such as a pork chop

explanation.surface: A butcher's instruction to slice a thick piece of meat in a hurry.
explanation.definitionFit: Chop-chop is an informal exhortation meaning hurry up, do it fast.

clue.text: Her pupil's tenth sloppy game

indicators.note: sloppy work is careless and disordered, so the preceding words are jumbled

parts.note: the letters of these three words

explanation.surface: A teacher grades her pupil's tenth piece of work as careless.
explanation.definitionFit: Hunt the slipper is a children's party game in which a shoe is passed secretly round a circle while one player tries to find it.

clue.text: Look for expert with a universal remedy

parts.note: to pan for gold is to search for it
an ace is a skilled expert
'with' joins; the a is taken as written

explanation.surface: Seek out a specialist who has a cure for everything.
explanation.definitionFit: A panacea is a supposed cure-all for every ailment or problem.

clue.text: Army store, or so it's said

indicators.note: this signals that the word for store counts only as it is spoken

parts.note: a hoard is a hidden store

explanation.surface: An army surplus store, or so people say.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Army store' reads as one shop; split it: Army is the definition, store the word that is heard.
explanation.definitionFit: A horde is a large crowd or marauding band, loosely an army.

clue.text: Leader of party? Mention first choice

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: the initial of party
a mention of something is a reference to it

explanation.surface: Should the party leader be named as the top pick?
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark breaks the surface into two sentences; ignore it when assembling.
explanation.definitionFit: A preference is the option you favour above the rest.

clue.text: Who, to boot, cared for sick?

definitions.text: Who, to boot, cared for sick?

parts.words: Who, to boot, cared for sick?
parts.note: surface reading: someone who, in addition, nursed the ill
setter's reading: the Time Lord Doctor Who, and 'to boot' read as unshod, without boots

explanation.surface: Asking which person also looked after the ill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To boot' normally means also; here it suggests going without boots. Doctor Who is the BBC science-fiction hero. The real figure was a rural paramedic in Mao's China.
explanation.definitionFit: Barefoot doctors were Chinese farm workers given basic medical training to care for villagers.

clue.text: Clan leader one English newspaper featured in series

indicators.note: to be featured in something is to appear inside it

parts.note: a chain of events is a series
the Roman numeral for one
standard abbreviation
the Financial Times

explanation.surface: A Highland clan chief is profiled in an English paper's series.
explanation.walkthrough: The FT is the Financial Times, the pink London business paper.
explanation.definitionFit: A chieftain is the head of a Scottish clan or tribe.

clue.text: Regular returned holding right cheek

indicators.note: returned means sent back, so the word is read from end to start

parts.note: regular as in steady, even
standard abbreviation

explanation.surface: A regular soldier came back clutching his right cheek.
explanation.definitionFit: Nerve here means impudence or brazen boldness, the same as cheek.

clue.text: Go-getter abroad, eastern salesman wearing this French material

indicators.note: abroad suggests scattered far and wide, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters of the word
standard abbreviation

indicators.note: the salesman is wearing the next words, so they are wrapped around him

parts.note: ce is French for this
a rep is a sales representative

explanation.surface: An ambitious eastern salesman abroad shows off French fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: Georgette crepe is a thin, sheer silk or crepe fabric named after a French dressmaker.

clue.text: Shoot tough old birds? They help one to live

parts.note: to pot is to shoot game
boilers are old hens fit only for boiling

explanation.surface: A hunter shoots stringy old fowl to survive.
explanation.walkthrough: A boiler is an old chicken, too tough to roast. The definition is cryptic: these are works produced just to earn a living.
explanation.definitionFit: Potboilers are books or art made quickly for money, keeping the creator fed.

clue.text: Evident in extra time

indicators.note: 'in' says the answer is found within the longer phrase, the rest cut away

parts.note: overtime is extra time worked or played

explanation.surface: Something obviously visible during extra time in a match.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is the opening of the word for extra time, with the closing letters dropped.
explanation.definitionFit: Overt means open and plainly visible, not hidden.

clue.text: Efficient secret agent

definitions.meaning: second meaning: a spy or undercover worker

explanation.surface: Describing a capable spy.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective it means in force or working; as a noun it is a spy or agent.

clue.text: Carry out appliance

definitions.meaning: first meaning: put into effect, as a verb
second meaning: a tool or utensil, as a noun

explanation.walkthrough: It sounds like removing a kitchen gadget; the two parts are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is a verb meaning to execute a plan and a noun meaning a tool.

clue.text: Copper lacking moral principles joined with Capone?

parts.note: base means low and immoral
met as in came together
'with' joins; Al Capone was the Chicago gangster

explanation.surface: A corrupt policeman who teamed up with Al Capone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' wants to be a policeman, fitting the gangster theme; it is the metal.
explanation.definitionFit: Copper is a base metal, one that is common and corrodes, unlike gold or silver.

clue.text: Altar? I'm nervous of marriage

indicators.note: a nervous person is jittery and unsettled, so the letters are shaken up

parts.note: the letters of these two words

explanation.surface: A bride confesses jitters about the altar and wedlock.
explanation.definitionFit: Marital is the adjective relating to marriage or a married couple.

clue.text: Most important one caught, a subject of conversation

parts.note: top as in chief
the Roman numeral for one
C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: The key person was arrested, and everyone is talking about it.
explanation.definitionFit: A topic is a theme or matter that people discuss.

clue.text: Run out stopping kid getting flower

indicators.note: to stop something is to plug it, sitting in its middle

parts.note: to kid is to tease
the cricket abbreviation for run
O for out, as in a scorecard or the letter's shape

explanation.surface: A runner was dismissed, halting a child who was picking a bloom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kid' is the verb, to joke with, not a child.
explanation.definitionFit: The tea rose is a variety of garden rose with a scent likened to tea.

clue.text: Mean map used by alien from Venus, perhaps

parts.note: mean as in low-grade, inferior
a plan is a map of a building or area
'used by' joins; ET is the film alien

explanation.surface: A shoddy chart carried by a visitor from Venus.
explanation.walkthrough: The alien looks like the subject of the surface, but 'from' is a link and Venus, with 'perhaps', is the definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Venus orbits closer to the Sun than Earth, which astronomers call an inferior planet, Mercury being the other.

clue.text: Girl's name, favourite, read out

parts.note: F marks the favourite in racing odds, as in 2-1F

indicators.note: out as in disordered or awry, so the word before it is rearranged

parts.note: the letters of the word

explanation.surface: A favourite girl's name is announced to the room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Read out' looks like one phrase meaning recited, but 'out' alone is the rearranging signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Freda is a female first name, a form of Frederica or Winifred.

clue.text: Colour of yard in prison

indicators.note: in places one item within the other

parts.note: the can is slang for jail
Y is the abbreviation for yard

explanation.surface: The paint colour of a prison exercise yard.
explanation.definitionFit: Cyan is a greenish-blue hue, one of the printing primaries.

clue.text: Level before start of this competition

parts.note: level as in flat, even

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter

parts.note: the initial of this

explanation.surface: The scores were level before this contest started.
explanation.definitionFit: An event is a single contest within a sports meeting.

clue.text: People in general seen round shady place in New York street

indicators.note: round means encircling, so one word goes around the other

parts.note: they, as in 'they say', means people at large
a bower is a leafy, shaded retreat

explanation.surface: Everyone gathers round a shady corner of a Manhattan street.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bowery is a street and district in lower Manhattan, once notorious for flophouses.

clue.text: Humble dramatist's young children

parts.note: small as in lowly, humble
Christopher Fry was an English verse dramatist

explanation.surface: A modest playwright's little ones.
explanation.walkthrough: Christopher Fry wrote The Lady's Not for Burning.
explanation.definitionFit: Small fry is an informal term for little children, as well as unimportant people.

clue.text: Church worker attacked holding cross

parts.note: set on means attacked
X is a cross shape

explanation.surface: A church employee was assaulted while carrying a crucifix.
explanation.definitionFit: A sexton looks after a church building and graveyard, often digging graves.
